samples.summary: `does not toggle without a callback` asserts nothing about toggling — it is a duplicate of the disabled-attribute test
samples.evidence: The test dispatches a click on the checkbox and then only asserts `preview.el.querySelector('input')?.hasAttribute('disabled') === true` — the same assertion already made by `renders a disabled checkbox for task-list items without a toggle` (preview.test.ts:42-57). Nothing observes whether a toggle happened, and with `onToggleTask` undefined there is no observable to capture one, so the test passes regardless of whether the click path is inert (e.g. if `onTaskClick` were unconditionally attached and started mutating the DOM, or `e.preventDefault()` were dropped, this test would still be green). The stated behaviour ("the click is inert") has no assertion behind it.

samples.summary: `does nothing when the block cannot move` cannot distinguish the guarded implementation from an unguarded one
samples.evidence: `indentList`/`outdentList` guard with `if (step > 0)` / `if (step < 0)` (list-commands.ts:261-270). With the guards removed, `shift(view, 0)` recomputes an identical prefix for every line, `replacePrefixes` pushes no changes, and the doc is unchanged — so `expect(view.state.doc.toString()).toBe('- a\n- b')` holds either way. The test asserts an outcome that is true independent of the guard it appears to cover (no assertion on transaction count / undo depth / selection).

samples.summary: No test that `noteCheckboxInput` is actually wired into the editor, nor that typing in a real editor performs the rewrite
samples.evidence: checkbox-input.test.ts never mounts the real editor: its `type()` helper reaches into `view.state.facet(EditorView.inputHandler)` and invokes the handler directly, so it tests the handler in isolation. Nothing asserts the extension is present in `initialize`'s extension list (editor.ts:373) or that a keystroke through the editor path yields `- [ ] `. Removing line 373 would keep every test green. I grepped for `noteCheckboxInput` across **/*.{ts,tsx} (only checkbox-input.ts/.test.ts and editor.ts) and read editor.test.ts's new task-click test.

samples.summary: The new `list` / `canIndent` / `canOutdent` fields of `computeActiveFormats` are never asserted
samples.evidence: commands.test.ts only asserts `.bold`, `.italic`, `.link` (lines 55-70). `computeListState` is exercised directly in list-commands.test.ts, but nothing checks that `computeActiveFormats` surfaces those three new fields, so a mis-wired mapping (e.g. `canIndent: list.canOutdent`) would not fail any test. Grepped `canIndent|list:` across packages/notes/src.

samples.summary: The `note-tasks-interactive` root class — the only hook the new CSS keys off — has no test
samples.evidence: preview.ts:198-203 conditionally appends `note-tasks-interactive`, and notes-preview.css:346-347 depends on it for the pointer cursor. No test in preview.test.ts asserts the class is present with a callback or absent without one (grepped `note-tasks-interactive` repo-wide: only preview.ts, the CSS, and the task doc). Nothing else in the suite would catch the class being dropped or misspelled.

samples.summary: Untested branches of the list parser/indent model: `*`/`+`/`1)` markers, and indenting under a deeper preceding item
samples.evidence: LIST_RE accepts `[-*+]` and `\d{1,9}[.)]` (list-commands.ts:32) but every test fixture uses only `- ` and `1. `, so `kindOf` for `1)` and bullets written with `*`/`+` are unexercised. `indentStep`'s `above.indent.length > top.indent.length` branch (list-commands.ts:160-163, target = above.indent.length) has no fixture either — all indent tests use a same-level sibling. A regression in those branches would pass CI.

samples.summary: The five new toolbar controls (pressed state from `formats.list`, disabled state from `canIndent`/`canOutdent`) have no test
samples.evidence: There is no notes-toolbar test file — packages/frontend/src/app/notes contains only yorkie-note-store.test.ts and notes-undo-integration.test.ts (Glob of that directory), and grep for `NotesToolbar` finds only notes-toolbar.tsx and notes-detail.tsx. The acceptance criteria "Indent / Outdent buttons, disabled when the line cannot be indented" is therefore only covered at the `computeListState` level, not at the wiring level (a swapped `onToggle` or wrong `pressed` expression would ship green). Noted as minor since the component was untested before this change too.

samples.summary: Checkbox input handler untested for a non-empty selection and for text following the cursor
samples.evidence: Every case in checkbox-input.test.ts mounts a bare cursor at end of line. The handler's change spans `{from: line.from, to}` where `to` is the selection end (checkbox-input.ts:38-40), so a non-collapsed selection or trailing text after the box (`'[ ]x'` with the caret at 3) take untested paths that can delete or reflow content. Also untested: the documented "one undo unit" claim (no history assertion).

finding.summary: `does not toggle without a callback` asserts nothing about toggling — it is a duplicate of the disabled-attribute test
finding.evidence: The test dispatches a click on the checkbox and then only asserts `preview.el.querySelector('input')?.hasAttribute('disabled') === true` — the same assertion already made by `renders a disabled checkbox for task-list items without a toggle` (preview.test.ts:42-57). Nothing observes whether a toggle happened, and with `onToggleTask` undefined there is no observable to capture one, so the test passes regardless of whether the click path is inert (e.g. if `onTaskClick` were unconditionally attached and started mutating the DOM, or `e.preventDefault()` were dropped, this test would still be green). The stated behaviour ("the click is inert") has no assertion behind it.

verdict.reason: Verified in the working tree. `does not toggle without a callback` (preview.test.ts:107-117) dispatches a click on the task checkbox but its sole assertion is `hasAttribute('disabled') === true`, which `render()` sets unconditionally when `onToggleTask` is absent (preview.ts:281-285) and which no click path can alter. The assertion is therefore true whether or not the click is inert: removing the attach guard at preview.ts:234 so `onTaskClick` ran unconditionally (calling e.preventDefault() at :264 and no-op `this.onToggleTask?.()` at :265) would leave this test green. No callback, spy, checked-state, or defaultPrevented observable is captured, so the named behaviour has no assertion behind it. The same assertion is already covered per-checkbox by `renders a disabled checkbox for task-list items without a toggle` (preview.test.ts:45-58; reviewer's 42-57 is a small line drift, not a misdescription). Vacuous coverage of a real branch — squarely in the test-adequacy lane and major by its rubric.
